newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes higher on primary auction.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes higher on primary auction.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rates closed 70 basis points higher on Wednesday at 23.20 percent in response to a greater-than-expected drop in primary rates from Tuesday's auction, traders said.
Money market analysts said Tuesday night's sharp fall in primary rates cut real returns substantially and indicates rates may be bottoming out.
"Real returns on the (benchmark) 28-day Cetes fell sharply and it is not likely that they'll keep falling in the current situation, with upside pressure on U.S. long bond yields," said an analyst.
Primary rates on one-month paper fell 201 basis points to 23.46 percent on Tuesday.
"We expected paper to be traded at lower levels, but volume was low. Traders are not motivated and the market is seeking to validate the new primary yield curve," a trader said.

Analysts estimated that real returns on the 28-day Cete after the new primary rates now stand at an annualized 7.66 percent, taking into account August's low inflation figures, compared with 9.8 percent after the prior auction. Trading volume was very thin for government instruments in the term market.
"It was a very strange market. There are dealers who suddenly step in to buy and stop rates going up," another trader said.
Government 28-day paper rates went against the overnight trend and closed 60 basis points down at 23.55 percent. Overnight bank paper closed 40 basis points up at 24.70 percent.
Banco de Mexico earlier injected 4.754 billion pesos to offset liquidity shortages in the secondary market by auctioning three credits with rates of between 24.76 and 25.49 percent.

Traders said a liquidity shortfall, first estimated at 7.394 billion pesos because of credits falling due, was cut by government spending of three billion pesos. Credit maturities totaling one billion pesos are expected on Thursday
